title: Sections, Articles, and Asides
summary: Choose article, section, and aside when the content has a clear semantic role.

sketchBlocks.title: Use article for content that can stand on its own
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use `
` for a self-contained piece of content such as a news story, blog post, review, or forum post. ```html

Science Club Launches Weather Balloon

The team collected temperature data above the city.

``` Read this example line by line: article opens the independent story, the heading names that story, the paragraph supplies its content, and the closing article ends the self-contained item. Do not choose article just because you need a generic box.

sketchBlocks.title: Use section for a thematic group of related content
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use `
` when a part of the page forms a meaningful theme and usually deserves its own heading. ```html

Upcoming Events

Open lab — Wednesday

``` Read this example line by line: section starts the themed group, the h2 names the theme, the paragraph belongs to that theme, and the closing section finishes the group. If no semantic meaning exists, do not replace every generic wrapper with section automatically.

sketchBlocks.title: Use aside for complementary content
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use `
` for information related to nearby content but not required to understand the main content. Examples include related links, a short author note, or a sidebar reminder. ```html

Related workshop

Join the study-skills session on Tuesday.

``` Read this example line by line: aside opens the complementary region, the heading identifies it, the paragraph provides related information, and the closing aside ends that secondary content.

quizDraft.title: Choose the self-contained element
quizDraft.prompt: A school site publishes one student-written news story that could be shared by itself. Which element best represents that story?
quizDraft.hint: Choose the element whose content can stand on its own.

help.hint_1: Section groups a theme inside a larger page.
help.hint_2: Choose article for the independent story.

quizDraft.title: Identify appropriate semantic containers
quizDraft.prompt: Which two uses are semantically appropriate?
quizDraft.hint: Choose based on the meaning of the content.

help.concept: Section and aside describe different relationships to surrounding content.
help.hint_1: A themed group can be a section.
help.hint_2: Complementary related information can be an aside.

options: Use <section> for a named group of upcoming events.
Use <aside> for related resources next to an article.
Use <article> for every paragraph because article is more semantic than p.
Use <section> only to create visual spacing.

quizDraft.title: Build a headed section
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange the tokens into a valid section with a heading and paragraph.
quizDraft.hint: The section wrapper contains both pieces of content.

help.concept: A section commonly begins with a heading that identifies its theme.
help.hint_2: Close section after the related paragraph.

quizDraft.title: Complete the complementary region
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the markup that best fills the blank after an article with related but secondary information.
quizDraft.hint: The content supports the article without belonging to its main story.

help.hint_1: Article would imply another self-contained story.
